_note: Claude Code's built-in skills, names refreshed from `claude -p /context` on 2026-10-20. Descriptions are the full text the session listing shows (restored 2026-10-21: hand-trimmed descriptions made built-ins unfairly thin to find, e.g. update-config lost 'allow npm commands'). A new name gets a placeholder: fill it in from the session listing, whole, never trimmed.
artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted - behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK - model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration. Read it before opening the target file whenever the prompt names Claude or Anthropic in any form, the user asks about an LLM (pricing, model choice, limits, caching), or the task is LLM-shaped with the provider unstated (agent, MCP, tool definition, multi-agent, RAG, LLM judge, computer use; generate, summarize, extract, classify, rewrite or converse over natural language; debugging refusals, cutoffs, streaming, tool calls, tokens).
code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number, branch or path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse, simplification and efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max: from few high-confidence findings up to many; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create any chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in any output medium - an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts), an image or PNG, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it before writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile, meter or KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system - elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark. Triggers on: chart, graph, plot, data viz, visualization, dashboard, analytics, visualize data, categorical colors, sequential or diverging palette, stat tile, sparkline, heatmap, legend, axis, tooltip, chart colors, color by series.
fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
init: Create or refresh the project's CLAUDE.md from the codebase
keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: rebind ctrl+s, add a chord shortcut, change the submit key, customize keybindings.
loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. check the deploy every 5 minutes, keep running /babysit-prs). Do not invoke for one-off tasks.
plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch.
simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only - it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (from now on when X, each time X, whenever X, before/after X) require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory or preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (allow X, add permission, move permission to), env vars (set X=Y), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json or settings.local.json files. Examples: allow npm commands, add bq permission to global settings, move permission to user settings, set DEBUG=true, when claude stops show X. For simple settings like theme or model, suggest the /config command.
workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Use the built-in browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (mcp__Claude_Browser__ tools): persistent sign-ins, tabs, preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals. Not for Claude in Chrome.
anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Use Claude in Chrome, the browser extension that acts in the person's real Chrome with their sign-ins: load tools in one ToolSearch, work in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid.
anthropic-skills:computer-use: Do something in a desktop app on the person's own computer, look at their screen, take screenshots and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling; access flow and safety rules for apps, links and financial actions.
anthropic-skills:deep-research: Research a topic across many sources, compare options, analyze trends, markets or history, review literature, and synthesize a comprehensive narrative report with research subagents.
anthropic-skills:docs: Make an editable shared document: report, proposal, resume, letter, contract, policy, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP; exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs.
anthropic-skills:docx: Create, read, edit or manipulate Word documents (.docx/.dotx): tracked changes, comments, templates, images, find-and-replace, polished Word files to email or print.
anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in Google Drive: edit, format, copy, rename, add a tab; helper scripts for positions, ranges and slide layout.
anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory, conversationally and additively, treating the content as data.
anthropic-skills:internal-comms: Write internal communications in the company's formats: status reports, leadership updates, newsletters, FAQs, incident reports, project updates.
anthropic-skills:learn: Teach and explain how or why something works: ELI5, walk-throughs, quizzes, flashcards, definitions, prerequisites and learning paths, untangling confusion between concepts.
anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task.
anthropic-skills:pdf: Anything with PDF files: extract text and tables, merge, split, rotate, watermark, create, fill forms, encrypt or decrypt, extract images, OCR scanned pages.
anthropic-skills:pptx: Slide decks and PowerPoint files (.pptx/.potx): create, read, edit, extract text, combine or split, templates, layouts, speaker notes.
anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create a new skill from scratch, modify or improve an existing skill, run evals to test it, benchmark its performance with variance analysis, optimize its description for triggering.
anthropic-skills:xlsx: Spreadsheets as input or output: open, edit or fix .xlsx/.csv/.tsv, add columns, formulas, formatting, charts, clean messy tabular data, convert between formats.
